item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00189","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C14","C10","C04"],"selected_candidate_label":"C14","confidence":0.82,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C14 plausibly supplied a material template for the child: both presidential letters address the same steel labor conflict through a sequence emphasizing the national importance of uninterrupted steel production, urging the parties to resume or continue operations, and directing labor and management toward immediate meetings and settlement. The child adapts that established appeal-and-conference structure to the post-injunction circumstances of May 1952. C10 and C04 contain closely related earlier machinery, but C14 is the closest combination of language and operative structure.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"The continued production of steel is of critical importance... I therefore request you... to do everything you can to restore the steel plants to full operation as quickly as possible","parent_excerpt":"Because of the vital importance of continued steel production... I also request the parties to extend the period for continued work and operations","explanation":"Both frame continued steel output as a vital public interest and use that premise to request uninterrupted or restored operations."},{"child_excerpt":"I also request you to meet with me... to begin further conferences seeking an immediate settlement of the issues between the companies and the union.","parent_excerpt":"I now request the parties immediately to meet in collective bargaining sessions... promptly to resolve their differences.","explanation":"The operative request is substantially parallel: immediate labor-management meetings aimed at prompt settlement."}]}
